concepts.name: Realm Management (online-beratung)
concepts.summary: The repo carries the exported Keycloak realm definition (realm.json) for the 'online-beratung' realm — clients, roles, and auth settings imported into Keycloak on deployment.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Deployment (caritas namespace)
concepts.summary: Keycloak runs on k3s in the 'caritas' namespace: keycloak-deployment.yaml (pod spec), keycloak-service.yaml (service), ingress.yaml (routing). DEPLOYMENT.md documents the procedure and prerequisites.

concepts.name: HTTP Access Mode (SSL requirement disabled)
concepts.summary: Keycloak requires HTTPS by default; in ORISO, nginx terminates TLS and internal services talk HTTP. configure-http-access.sh must run after every deployment to disable the SSL requirement for all realms, otherwise authentication fails with 'HTTPS required'.

concepts.name: Realm Backup
concepts.summary: backup/realm-backup.sh exports the 'online-beratung' realm from the running Keycloak pod (kubectl exec) into timestamped backups in the repo's backup directory.

concepts.name: E-mail OTP second factor (vendored otp-config SPI)
concepts.summary: E-mail second-factor login is implemented by the vendored ORISO-Keycloak otp-config SPI. OtpMailAuthenticator answers direct-grant token requests and delegates the submitted code to MailOtpVerifier. OtpMailFormAuthenticator handles browser login forms and delegates submitted codes to the same MailOtpVerifier. The verifier invalidates a valid credential and counts invalid attempts through the credential service. MemoryOtpService creates codes with a configurable lifetime (900 seconds by default), and checks expiry, invalidation and the limit of three failed validations. These are source-level responsibilities; this graph does not establish deployed authentication behavior. ADR-013 records the original vendoring under ORISO-Helm; the reviewed current classes are under ORISO-Keycloak.

concepts.name: otp-config REST API (how UserService reaches the 2FA SPI)
concepts.summary: RealmOtpResourceProviderFactory registers the realm resource as otp-config. RealmOtpResourceProvider declares GET fetch-otp-setup-info/{username}, PUT setup-otp/{username}, DELETE delete-otp/{username}, PUT send-verification-mail/{username} and POST setup-otp-mail/{username}, with service-session authentication before each operation. These are the Keycloak SPI endpoints used by the UserService second-factor client; they are source declarations, not runtime verification. ADR-013 is historical architectural context for the original ORISO-Helm location.

flows.name: Deploy & Configure
flows.summary: Apply the Kubernetes manifests (deployment, service, ingress) → wait for the Keycloak pod to become ready → run configure-http-access.sh to disable the SSL requirement → realm available for the platform.

flows.name: Backup & Restore Realm
flows.summary: realm-backup.sh exports the realm from the running pod to a timestamped file; realm.json is the canonical import used to restore or re-provision the realm.
